artifact_or_test_id: ad hoc contention probe on the session scratch copy (ac4root), 2026-10-26
command_or_fixture: Scratch copy of the live store and docs/waves; a second process holds index_source_guard(wait=True) for 40 s while four injected-time monitor ticks run with a _find_wave_md spy
counterexample_or_failure_condition: While another process holds index_source_guard, closed waves never park and each quiet period costs seconds of lookups.
expected: Bounded cost under retryable conditions, as Requirement 3 states
known_bad_detection_method: Contention probe with a second process holding the guard reproduced the unparked closed waves and the per-quiet-period lookup pass
limitations: Single server; the cost scales with the number of servers and lasts only while a build holds the guard
observed: past quiet: 9.73 s, 27 lookups, index_source_busy; next tick: 0.03 s, 0 lookups; past quiet again: 7.38 s, 22 lookups; only the 5 unknown ids parked. Cost bounded to one pass per 120 s quiet period while contention lasts. No ambiguous or reopened-sealed row exists in today's data.
proposition: Persistent retryable conditions still cost one full wave lookup per eligible wave per quiet period: index_source_busy while an index build holds the guard (reported before the closed status is read), and by the same path an ambiguous id raising from _find_wave_md or a reopened sealed row reporting already_current.
safety_and_authorization: Scratch copy only; the live store and wave records were not touched

disposition_rationale: Within the bound Requirement 3 states and accepts; avoiding it means reading the closed status before taking the locks or caching wave resolution, which changes lock ordering or resolution semantics for a cost that ends with the build. Worth a later look if index builds prove long or frequent.
promotion_trigger: Field reports or measurements showing index builds hold the guard long or often enough that servers stay hot, or an ambiguous or reopened-sealed pending row appearing in real data
